about.title: Redlands Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Redlands sits where the I-10 meets everyday errands. The same freeway that carries commuters through town also feeds Orange Street, Alabama Street and Lugonia Avenue, and those four corridors show up most often in the city's public collision records. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, those records list 477 injury collisions inside Redlands, with 671 people hurt and five lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the week's traffic is slow to thin out. If one of those numbers now describes you, the next few weeks matter. California gives most crash victims two years to file, but claims involving a city or county vehicle can carry a window as short as six months. Insurers know that, and they often move quickly to request a recorded statement. You are not required to give one. LawProactive is a free service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who handles Redlands car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless money is recovered.

whyChoose.title: Why Redlands Drivers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines here are shorter than most people think
items.desc: Two years sounds generous until you learn that a claim against a government entity, such as a Redlands city vehicle or a Caltrans maintenance truck on the I-10, may need to be filed within six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to you.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not close the door
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by your share of blame rather than erased by it. Even if you rolled through a yellow on Lugonia Avenue, you may still have a claim.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and loss of normal life. Our connection service is free, and you owe the attorney nothing unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurer called and wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You have no legal obligation to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink or deny your claim, even when you are simply being polite. Speak with an attorney first, and let them handle communication with the other side.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the I-10 near the Alabama Street exit and my car is already at a yard. What evidence can I still save?
items.answer: Quite a bit. Photograph the vehicle before it is repaired or scrapped, keep every medical bill and discharge note, and write down the names of any witnesses or the CHP report number while it is fresh. Dashcam footage, phone photos from the scene and even your own texts about the crash can all help an attorney reconstruct what happened on the freeway.

items.question: How does LawProactive work, and what does it cost me?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured people in Redlands with an independent personal injury attorney who has agreed to review their case. That attorney works on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery, and you are never charged for the connection itself.
